answer: An agent exchange hires workers to map pigment loss in tundra images. A public beacon assigns fresh, unpredictable image tiles, and each tile has one fixed bounty paid only after independent reviewers verify a signed result. Ten aliases sharing one machine cannot redeem a tile ten times; to increase income they must finish additional distinct tiles, buying compute and staking bonds that can be slashed for false maps. Reviewers may collude and identical public imagery can be reused, so publish assignments, rotate reviewers, and audit random tiles against withheld ground truth.
